findings.area: Private engine keys and shared internal symbols
findings.staticReachability: Startup: process exit state/errors; later CJS, VM, source maps, clone and messaging.
findings.classification: Implementable engine property-key semantics plus one shared native symbol registry.
findings.requiredContract: Node creates V8 Private keys and exports the exact same identities through util.privateSymbols and per-context arguments. Upstream JS uses ordinary bracket syntax with these engine keys; native owners use GetPrivate/SetPrivate. Keys must remain hidden from ordinary reflection, consistent between JS/native, and coherent for object lifecycle, realms, proxies and transfer admission. Ordinary Symbol values are not equivalent. Internal public-ish symbols from symbols binding are a separate registry and need exact sharing.
findings.resetDisposition: Implement the native private-name registry in SpiderMonkey and use genuine hidden private names; the old createCloneModeSymbol uses NewPrivateName already and is a reusable foothold. Replace per-adapter ordinary Symbol/WeakMap substitutions by the owning engine/binding contract, preserving unmodified JS.

findings.area: Error capture, CallSites and lazy stack formatting
findings.staticReachability: Startup: realm installs formatter; error construction/formatting widely reachable.
findings.classification: Engine hooks required, with unchanged JS formatting policy above them.
findings.requiredContract: Node installs a prepareStackTrace callback during realm bootstrap. Engine error creation/capture must retain actual frame identities, implement Error.captureStackTrace(error, boundary), stackTraceLimit and structured CallSite methods, then invoke the callback with the correct error realm/global when stack is accessed. JS formatter/source-map helpers do not produce missing engine frames or capture semantics. Cross-realm policy, hidden frames, source positions, async frames, descriptors and reentrancy are observable.
findings.resetDisposition: Implement the native errors binding and actual SpiderMonkey Error/stack hooks before replacing guarded internal/errors source with its unchanged body. The existing assertion-only native source capture is useful input, not public Error.captureStackTrace. Never invent frames or keep the guard that suppresses required upstream behavior.

findings.area: Microtasks, nextTick and rejection event ownership
findings.staticReachability: Startup: node.js installs task queue; every asynchronous API.
findings.requiredContract: task_queue binding owns actual microtask enqueue/checkpoint, mutable tickInfo shared state, tick callback and promise rejection callback. Upstream task_queues.js interleaves nextTicks, microtasks and rejection delivery in a specified loop. Native callback scopes must cooperate with that loop; draining the outer browser queue is not equivalent. Promise reject events must refer to actual guest promises and correct handler-added timing.
findings.resetDisposition: Implement the full binding using the guest engine job queue and native callback entry/exit scopes. Keep upstream task_queues.js and process/promises.js unchanged. Audit exception unwinding and nested checkpoints before any broad module support claim.

findings.area: ModuleWrap, synthetic builtins and real ESM graph
findings.staticReachability: ModuleWrap constructor/prototype needed at startup; synthetic builtin facades and source modules used on import.
findings.classification: Engine module embedding contract, including potentially missing language features.
findings.requiredContract: realm.js imports ModuleWrap unconditionally and nulls its prototype. Builtin ESM facades require real synthetic modules, named live exports, instantiate and immediate evaluate; full ESM requires source module requests, attributes, source/defer/evaluation phases, namespace identity, link/evaluation status, dynamic import/import.meta callbacks, graph cycles and TLA rejection. Node require(ESM) requires synchronous evaluateSync behavior for admissible graphs.
findings.resetDisposition: Provide one genuine SpiderMonkey module-record owner with exact binding-facing shape; existing engine source graph/synthetic builtin work is a starting point. If the guest parser lacks a standardized phase syntax requested by user code, it is an engine feature gap to implement or explicitly review—not permission to rewrite upstream loader source.
findings.evidenceLimits: No parser/module execution probes run. Full phase, synthetic module and sync/TLA parity has not been established by static inspection.

findings.area: VM contexts, compilation and watchdog control
findings.staticReachability: Public node:vm and loader customization; not required to execute every basic builtin.
findings.classification: Implementable realms/native embedding with substantive lifecycle and safety requirements.

Returning the main global or using JS eval does not implement VM isolation or native constructor behavior.

findings.area: Snapshots, V8 caches, heap/optimizer and inspector
findings.staticReachability: Snapshot state binding startup-reachable; heap/profiler/inspector public APIs lazy/config-dependent.
findings.classification: Mixed: truthful startup state is implementable; exact V8-specific observability needs explicit boundary decisions.
findings.requiredContract: startup_snapshot always imports mksnapshot binding and reads actual isBuildingSnapshotBuffer, even when snapshot creation is off. Heap space names, V8 optimizer flags, CPU/heap profiler protocols, cachedDataVersionTag and serialized V8 snapshots reflect a concrete engine and cannot be fabricated for SpiderMonkey. Inspector exposes real protocol session and debugger semantics; declaring hasInspector=false is truthful only if capability genuinely absent and remains a documented non-pass.
findings.resetDisposition: Supply truthful snapshot-disabled state for an ordinary non-snapshot build while preserving upstream namespace/errors. Decompose node:v8 and inspector into API-specific implementable equivalents/protocols vs literal V8 artifacts that need user-reviewed exclusions or much larger backends. Never exempt all node:v8, because E06/E12 contain implementable behavior.
findings.evidenceLimits: These are engine architecture differences, not claims of SpiderMonkey defects. Exact API exclusions are proposed decisions, not authorized omissions or conformance passes.

findings.area: Nested WebAssembly required by unchanged shipped JS dependencies
findings.staticReachability: Lazy fetch HTTP/1 parser and TypeScript transform; module Wasm imports; node:wasi.
findings.classification: Real execution backend prerequisite; cannot be replaced by repointing an existing native HTTP parser under unchanged bytes.
findings.requiredContract: configure.py includes bundled Undici/Amaro. Unchanged Undici HTTP/1 lazyllhttp throws without WebAssembly, compiles SIMD module with scalar fallback, and instantiates module/import callbacks synchronously. Amaro bundles Wasm bytes then creates Module/Instance synchronously. ESM translators also use WebAssembly.Module/Instance and source-phase module behavior. An outer host supports WebAssembly, but the guest JS global/API still needs its own correct execution boundary.
findings.resetDisposition: Keep a genuine guest nested-Wasm backend in scope and reflect its dependencies explicitly. It can be last for an initial CJS/streams/fs slice, but complete unchanged fetch HTTP/1 and TypeScript cannot be marked done before it. Native llhttp work remains useful for Node internal http_parser and cannot silently replace Undici own Wasm engine calls.

findings.area: Native addon imports are a distinct ABI boundary
findings.staticReachability: Only native .node addon import/load; regular builtin JS execution unaffected.
findings.classification: Native machine-code/addon ABI and embedding integration, not JS parser syntax.
findings.requiredContract: Unchanged CJS .node extension calls process.dlopen; ESM addon translation delegates to the same actual loader. Host native .node binaries and V8-linked addons cannot execute as Kandelo wasm guest code simply because JS modules are reused. N-API portability still needs a genuine supported guest side-module ABI, loader and object/lifetime implementation.
findings.resetDisposition: Preserve upstream loader code, report real loader failures, and make native addon format/ABI support an explicit scoped roadmap/boundary. Do not infer an addon capability from implementing core internalBinding exports.
findings.evidenceLimits: No native addon compatibility matrix or loader validation performed; this row prevents conflating C++ internal bindings with loading third-party native addons.
